text: For a family on four hundred dollars a month, every purchase is a decision. MamaPal gives that month a pal. Pal cares, Pal cuts, Pal claims. It runs on Claude and PayPal.

New in this version: hand Pal the whole month. It plans, finds real prices, and then a checker that is not the AI opens every link and redoes the math. In one real run for Maya, it caught a plan that would have left her baby a week without formula, and sent it back.

Anyone can open one of three fictional households, each as a private copy. This is Maya in Houston. Leo is four months old. Pal opens with the month: two hundred sixty dollars free, and the formula runs out in about four days.

Maya types what Instagram told her to buy: a forty-five dollar calming oil and a sixty dollar sleep sack. Pal says skip both: four dollars of zinc cream does the job. And because formula runs out in four days, it adds formula and diapers she did not ask for.
The card opens beside the conversation. Swap, swap, buy, buy, each with one line of why. Two hundred twenty-seven dollars asked, one thirty-six to pay, ninety-one intercepted.
One PayPal button, for exactly this cart. The sandbox buyer approves in PayPal's own window, the server captures the order, and the capture ID lands on the card. The pantry jumps to twenty-five days.
Now the month run. Pal takes stock: a hundred and twenty-four dollars free, twelve kept aside, twenty days to go. It plans five small things now and one for later.

It searches stores for real prices. Then the checker opens twelve links: four show the price on the store page, none are dead. Money, coverage to month end, and order all pass. Thirty-nine cents of AI time.
Every offer shows what the checker saw. The cart is twenty-four dollars, and one line is a free library story time. Pal never pays on its own. She does, in PayPal.

Pal claims: about twenty-two hundred dollars a month Maya likely qualifies for. Each rule comes with words copied from the official page, and the checker found them there. Texas SNAP: gross income at or below one hundred sixty-five percent of the poverty line.
A two-question brand survey pays two dollars back through PayPal Payouts, batch ID and all.
Every dollar lands in the ledger with its PayPal ID. Count every dollar, live every day. Try it yourself with the code MAYA-DEMO.
